segments.headline: A quick sketch
segments.narration: A line, a string, and a circle. A few quick pen strokes become a pendulum, right here in the captured room. The drawing itself opens into volume.

segments.headline: Motion generates the signal
segments.narration: Now the pendulum swings, and its angle generates this live waveform. I am not drawing a decorative wave. The moving object is the signal source. Change its amplitude or speed, and the curve changes with it.

segments.headline: A profile becomes a vase
segments.narration: Here is a second example. I sketch a profile beside an axis. Rotating that same curve sweeps out a wireframe vase. The original silhouette is still visible beside the volume.

segments.headline: Edit the curve, change the volume
segments.narration: Watch the waist become wider and narrower. Every meridian is computed from the same profile, so this is a geometric relationship, not a swap between finished models. The runnable version lets you adjust the width yourself.

segments.headline: Connect a sketch to a transform
segments.narration: For the third example, I draw an arrow and a coordinate frame, then connect them. The arrow appears in three dimensions. One rotation value drives both its orientation and this matrix.

segments.headline: One value, coupled representations
segments.narration: As the angle changes, the numbers and the shape stay synchronized. You can scrub that angle in the live project. These are three implemented, Chalktalk-inspired mechanisms, performed by the original Ryo avatar in today’s iPad scan.
